slides.title: Two thousand years of pharmacology, written in a language we stopped reading
bullets: The Asian medical canon — 神農本草經, 本草綱目, Charaka, Suśruta, al-Qānūn — is not folklore. It is a **structured, self-consistent, predictive system** with its own theory of drug action.
It also contains **ancient science**: 天工開物 on materials, 齊民要術 on fermentation, 夢溪筆談 on natural observation. These carry the process chemistry that medicine actually used.
Almost all computational work reads **modern English summaries** — exactly the layer where the encoded knowledge has been laundered out.
**1972**: a team read one word in a fourth-century line — *cold* water, not hot — and found artemisinin. The detail was a preparation instruction. Nobody had translated it into chemistry.
**Our question:** if we read the originals, does the theory still predict? And what does it let us propose? same molecule rendered. Caption: *one line of text → one compound.* ---
slides.visual: two columns — left, a page of 本草綱目 in 繁體 with a single line highlighted in cinnabar; right, the same molecule rendered. Caption: *one line of text → one compound.*
slides.speaker_note: The gap is not that we lack texts. It is that we read the wrong copies of them.

slides.title: We treat 四氣五味, 歸經 and rasa as a **predictive prior** — and we test it
bullets: "Cold, bitter, enters the Liver channel" is a **claim about chemistry and compartment** — polarity, volatility, thermolability, target tissue. So is Ayurvedic *vīrya* (hot/cold potency) and the six *rasa*.
We encode the property vector per drug and treat it as a **feature matrix**, not as colour: `nature · flavours · channels · direction · grade` / `rasa · guṇa · vīrya · vipāka · tridoṣa`.
That makes the framework **falsifiable**: shuffle the vectors, recompute, and see whether predictive power survives. If it does not, we report that with numbers.

**What this is not** — not a TCM knowledge graph (TCMSP, SymMap, ETCM, HERB do that better than we could in a week), not a TCM chatbot (ShenNong-TCM, HuatuoGPT, BianCang), not virtual screening. Everyone else has data or a chatbot. Three things are ours: **process language → chemistry**, **the theory tested as a prior**, and **a closed rule set bridged to mechanisms**.

Where the tradition **disagrees with itself** (edition-dependent channel assignments), we inherited the disagreement instead of resolving it silently. `MW · logP · target family · thermolability` — labelled *prediction*. Then a permutation arrow, labelled *null*. ---
slides.visual: a drug name on the left; the property vector as a row of chips; an arrow to `MW · logP · target family · thermolability` — labelled *prediction*. Then a permutation arrow, labelled *null*.
slides.speaker_note: If the theory predicts, we have a non-Western discovery engine. If it doesn't, we say so.

slides.title: We derived the corpus from axioms instead of collecting it
bullets: We wrote down the **axioms of ethnopharmacology and Asian pharmacology** first, then derived which data classes those axioms logically require, and only then sourced them.

Consequence: the registry is a **proof obligation**. Every tier exists because an axiom demanded it — an ontology (tier 0), a biology/chemistry substrate (tier 1), materia medica (tier 2), alchemy (tier 3), channels (tier 4), and structured ground truth (tier 5).
The **first-principles substrate is not "Western medicine"** — it is the interpretive layer that lets us say what a classical claim means in modern terms.
The Western herbal tradition is present only as a **labelled comparative control (≤ 3% of tokens)**, to test whether a finding is just an artefact of any large botanical corpus.
Every source carries title, author, date, URL, licence **and licence evidence**, tier, tradition, language. bottom. ---

slides.title: Trained from scratch on a laptop CPU in 45 minutes — and the weights are published
bullets: **8,719,616 parameters** (4,525,312 non-embedding) · 16,384-token vocabulary built for Classical Chinese and Sanskrit · `d_model` 256 · 6 layers · 4 heads · 512-token context · PyTorch 2.2.2, **no GPU**.

**200 steps × 8,192 = 1,638,400 tokens** in **2,711 s (45 min)** at 604 tokens/s, single thread. Train loss **6.3662**, validation **6.3901** (held-out perplexity 595.9); val curve 9.735 → 7.336 → 6.717 → 6.481 → **6.390**. The chart is that log, not a render.

**The weights: `shennong-mini-f16.gguf` = 18.05 MB** (18,054,560 bytes = 17.2 MiB), 56 tensors, sha256 `a67ad442…4cdb60`. That is **1.8 % of the 1 GB ceiling** — 55× less room than the constraint allowed.

**Stated flatly:** 1,638,400 tokens ÷ 8,719,616 params = **0.188 tokens/param ≈ 0.9 % of a compute-optimal budget**. This is a **pipeline proof, not a useful general model** — the honest claim is reproducibility, not capability.

**Run provenance:** the checkpoint trained on the 02:47 corpus snapshot (38.24 M chars / 16.69 M tokens) because the token cache was keyed on the tokeniser; the frozen corpus post-dates it. The bug is fixed, and we say so rather than letting the reader assume otherwise. logged loss curve (train solid, held-out dashed) from `training/runs/shennong-mini-r1/metrics.json`, with 18.05 MB and the 1 GB ceiling drawn to scale as a bar. is more model than it is.

slides.title: Four classical operations of Chinese pharmacy, used as the engineering vocabulary
bullets: **采 Cǎi — collect:** licence-audited acquisition, 繁/简 + IAST/Devanagari normalisation, 13-gram dedupe, entity extraction. → `corpus.jsonl`, `sources.yaml`

**制 Zhì — prepare:** drug names resolved across eras and scripts to modern taxa with confidence; process words compiled into a **chemistry operator** (炮/煅/淬/九蒸九曬 → hydrolysis, oxidation, volatilisation, complexation). We print the split we are least sure of: which steps are **load-bearing** (附子 炮制: diester → monester alkaloids) and which are **plausibly ritual**. → `lexicon_drugs.json`, `processing.csv`

**配 Pèi — combine:** taxon ↔ compound ↔ target ↔ indication; formula roles **君臣佐使**; and the **complete, faithful** interaction rule set — **16** canonical 相反 pairs + **11** 相畏 relations, which are what 十八反 and 十九畏 actually enumerate (the mnemonics count *drugs*, not pairs). Bridged, assay-annotated, verse-tagged. → `kg.json`
**使 Shǐ — deploy:** ranking, falsification plans, uncertainty, **drug candidates**, and the theory-predictivity experiment. → `drug_candidates.json`, `eval/report.json`
**One command per stage.** `make setup · corpus · tokenizer · train-mini · eval · app-data · workbench` runs from a clean clone on CPU. the specification. ---

slides.title: A prescription line from a 1406 formulary becomes a molecule with a name, a number and an assay
bullets: **The line.** *普濟方* (1406), the 前胡湯 entry: 「前胡汤治肺热咳嗽」 — "Qianhu decoction treats cough from lung heat." Verified verbatim, with a byte offset into the corpus (`ws_zh_pujifang:1190-1198`).

**The theory predicts the compartment.** 前胡 is 寒 · 苦 · 歸肺/肝/脾/膀胱 · 中品 — cold, bitter, entering **Lung**. The prediction is a lung-directed action, and the recorded indication is a cough syndrome. The framework named the organ; that is what makes it testable rather than decorative.

**The molecule.** Peucedanocoumarin I, **C₂₁H₂₄O₇**, **MW 388.42**, logP 4.6, HBD 0, HBA 7, TPSA 64.61 Å², 3 rings, 6 rotatable bonds. **4 of 4 Lipinski rules evaluated — passes; Veber passes.** Computed from the resolved SMILES.
**The assay.** Ca²⁺ flux (FLIPR) on TRPA1-expressing cells, then a recombinant cell line; go/no-go is reproducible engagement in two orthogonal assays plus selectivity over the nearest paralogue.

**Novelty is structural now, and it discriminates.** ECFP-style Tanimoto (radius 2) against the corpus's **23,172-structure table**, excluding each candidate's own compound and source plant: **42 distinct values, range 0.000–0.750, mean 0.283** — replaced a curated-name prior that gave every candidate 0.88 and made the rank order meaningless. It measures distance from documented phytochemistry, **not** therapeutic novelty, and the card says so. line highlighted in the source text, theory chips, molecular card with the computed descriptors, then the assay. drug-likeness verdict, a named target and the experiment that would test it. Nothing on this slide was typed by a human — it is the pipeline's output, and the provenance locator points into the corpus. ---

slides.title: One of five pre-registered axes survived its own test — and it is the mechanistic one
bullets: **Pre-registered.** Thresholds and the permutation construction were written into `docs/EVALUATION.md` *before* the numbers existed, so the test cannot be tuned into a positive. Each test: effect size, n, p, permutation null (theory vectors shuffled across drugs): · **四氣 (nature)** → compound polarity / thermolability · AUC **0.456** · **歸經 (channel tropism)** → target organ · **hit rate 0.075 vs 0.038 chance**, n = 2,059, **p = 0.008** · **五味 (flavours)** → receptor class · AUC **0.529** · **vīrya (Ayurvedic hot/cold)** → logP / thermolability · **n = 0**, not linkable: the 322 Sanskrit property rows have no Sanskrit→binomial lexicon, so the test cannot be run — reported as *not linkable*, not as *no effect* · **ṣaḍrasa (six tastes)** → action class · **n = 0**, not linkable (same lexicon gap)

**1 of 5** pre-registered tests beats its permutation null at p < 0.05 — and it is the most mechanistic one. **歸經 predicts target organ at 7.5 % vs a 3.8 % permutation mean over 2,059 (drug, use) pairs, p = 0.008, ≈2× chance.** 四氣 AUC 0.456 (p = 0.26) and 五味 AUC 0.529 (p = 0.78) show **no** signal; the two Ayurvedic tests are not linkable (n = 0). The honest reading is that channel tropism carries real but weak organ-level information, and the other classical axes we could operationalise did not survive our own test.

**And the null model refuses to flatter us.** Shuffling plant↔use edges changes the mean composite by **−0.026** [−0.042, −0.014] over 27 shuffles, n = 2,034 real vs 2,766 shuffled. That is *not* a collapse: it means the composite is **prior-dominated, not topology-sensitive**. We report it as a limitation of our own scorer instead of quoting a number that clears a threshold by construction.

**The negative controls stay honest.** 取象比類 (resemblance reasoning) is a hypothesis, not an assumption — on the real corpus it could not be computed (n = 0: too few colour-named drugs carry a recorded indication), and it is published at the bottom of the ranked list rather than quietly dropped. chip reading *predicts above chance* / *trend, not significant* / *no predictive signal*. about it. Both outcomes are the result. ---

slides.title: This corpus contains poisons, living heritage, and endangered species
bullets: **Medical safety is architecture, not a disclaimer.** No dosing, no diagnosis, no self-treatment, no preparation methods. The Ask surface **refuses by policy** — the dual-use screen is a hard gate in front of the generative surface, not a filter after it.

**Toxic materia medica, handled honestly.** Mercury, arsenic and lead drugs (丹, 輕粉, 雄黃, *bhasma*) are in the corpus as **toxicology data**. They appear in the output only as hazard analyses, with the safety annotation rendered on every view of them. We never help with them.

**Traditional Knowledge is living heritage, not ore.** Attribution to text, edition and where possible named author is in the data model. **Nagoya-Protocol** benefit-sharing, non-extractive framing, and a working opt-out: a community can withdraw a text and the corpus build honours it.

**Conservation is a direct output.** 犀角 → 水牛角 and 穿山甲 → 豬蹄甲 ranked by how load-bearing the ingredient is in its formula (**君 vs 佐**) — a substitution-priority list built from text that costs no animals. For calcined material the classical processing column *is* the argument: ash is ash.

**Name collisions are a public-health output.** 木通 vs 關木通: the 1596 marginal note already warns the two "resemble in form, differ in nature". Aristolochic acid is an **IARC Group 1** carcinogen. We rank colliding taxa by toxicity divergence. CITES badge and the 異名同物 collision graph. ---

slides.speaker_note: A system that mines this canon has to be able to say which of its own sources are poison.

slides.title: From shortlist to validated lead — what we need next
bullets: **Next 3 months:** wet-lab falsification of the top candidates, starting with the cheapest test — the processed-versus-raw comparison for 附子, where the mechanism is known and one LC-MS method decides it.

**Next 6 months:** cross-tradition prediction. Fit on 本草綱目, predict a held-out class recorded only in the Ayurvedic or Unani material. If the framework generalises across traditions, it is a discovery engine; if it doesn't, that is a paper too.
**Next 12 months:** extend to 農政全書 / 廣群芳譜 / full 救荒本草, and to Tibetan and Southeast Asian material where openly licensed editions exist. Every addition goes through the same licence audit.

**The ask:** · a **pharmacognosy / natural-products lab** partner for the first three assays; · a **practitioner and community review** panel, with attribution and benefit-sharing agreed *before* any wet work; · compute to train `shennong-0.5b` properly instead of by recipe.

**What we will give back, unconditionally:** the corpus audit, the method, the candidates, the negative results, and the Workbench — Apache-2.0, no gate, no network required. frame is the seal mark and the repo URL. ---
